key_insight: DanceOPD shows how to train one image generation model to handle text-to-image creation, local editing, and global editing without these skills fighting each other. Its core idea is to distill these capabilities on-policy so they can be composed more effectively in a single model.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the conflict between multiple image generation capabilities: improving editing often hurts text-to-image quality, and global editing can interfere with local editing. It tackles the challenge of unifying these abilities in one model without performance trade-offs.
method: Uses an on-policy generative field distillation strategy to align training with the model’s own generation behavior.
Learns a shared representation that composes text-to-image, local editing, and global editing more consistently.
Reduces capability interference by distilling from the current policy rather than relying on static or mismatched supervision.
impact: This matters because practitioners want one versatile image model instead of separate tools for generation and editing. DanceOPD points toward more capable, efficient multimodal image systems with fewer quality trade-offs.
visual_elements: A three-way capability diagram showing text-to-image, local editing, and global editing with overlap/conflict zones.
